definitions: Finite simple graph. Eulerian = connected with every vertex of even degree (equivalently, has a closed trail using every edge exactly once). 2-connected = at least 3 vertices and still connected after deleting any single vertex. Hamiltonian = has a cycle through every vertex.
ground_truth_witness: K_{2,4}, the complete bipartite graph with parts {u1,u2} and {w1,w2,w3,w4}; 6 vertices, 8 edges. Integer edge list with u1,u2 = 0,1 and w1..w4 = 2,3,4,5: [[0,2],[0,3],[0,4],[0,5],[1,2],[1,3],[1,4],[1,5]]. Every degree is even (4,4,2,2,2,2) and the graph is connected, so it is Eulerian, and it is 2-connected; but a cycle in a bipartite graph alternates sides, so a Hamiltonian cycle would need equal part sizes, and 2 != 4.
reference_authority: online-cited counterexample (MO/MSE/CS.SE/Wikipedia) with verify script, verified per partB_feasibility records
